(29/39/49/59/69/79/89) is a memory aid only; 99 is NOT an un- form (niranobboi).

lessons.label: Lesson 5 — Big Number Roots
lessons.title: Bengali Big Number Roots
notes: bn / lesson-5 — Bengali Big Number Roots (roots × multipliers 1-9)
Applied VERBATIM from the Bengali linguistics dataset review.
6 root families (hundreds, thousands, "millions", "billions", "trillions",
"quadrillions") × 9 multipliers = 54, PLUS the 2 standalone roots 10,000 and
AUTHENTIC South Asian lakh/koti grouping applied per the dataset: sho = 100,
single "million" word, so 10^6 = দশ লাখ (dosh lakh, 10 lakh); 10^9 = একশ কোটি
(eksho koti, 100 koti); 10^12 = এক লাখ কোটি (ek lakh koti); 10^15 = দশ কোটি কোটি
(dosh koti koti). Answer stacks native Bangla script | romanization via the
engine's " | " separator; prompts stay comma-formatted strings, byte-identical
to the reference deck.

lessons.label: Lesson 6 — Number Builder
lessons.title: Bengali Number Builder
notes: bn / lesson-6 — Bengali Number Builder
Applied VERBATIM from the Bengali linguistics dataset review. Keeps the
10-second reveal (revealMs: 10000). Each number is read in the South Asian
place-grouping (lakh / thousand / hundred / unit); the native form is stacked by
spoken place-group with " | " (rendered as stacked lines by the engine), and the
final line is the full romanization. The engine auto-shrinks long answers.
LB-45: lesson un-parked; 14 cards added (ids lesson-6.007–.020), 20 in all.
Cards are ordered by value, smallest first; ids keep the order they were
assigned in, so they are not in id order.
Line rule (one convention for every card): the script splits ONLY at the big
units — <lakh group> | <hajar group> | <hundreds + 1-99> — so at most 3 script
lines, then ONE romanization line (max 4 lines). A number under 1,000 is one
script line. LB-45 re-split cards .001–.003 to this rule (they used to split
the hundreds from the 1-99 word too); their words did not change.
Empty groups are silent: no "and", no "zero" (10,001 = দশ হাজার এক;
5,000,500 = পঞ্চাশ লাখ পাঁচশ). এক is always said (একশ, এক হাজার, এক লাখ).
The 1-99 part of every card is copied from Lesson 4, never built.
Hints spell লাখ as "lahk"; the romanization in the answer stays "lakh".
Indian grouping (how Bangladesh writes it; each comma is a spoken word):
10,00,001. Below 100,000 the two groupings look the same.
Spoken shortcuts NOT taught on cards (the standard form is the answer): দেড়শ
